findings.desc: multi-turn-fidelity: real-loop-agent.mjs:42 sets output=out.slice(0,400) where `out` is the raw JSON envelope from claude -p --output-format json (e.g. {"subtype":"success","result":"<agent text>","total_cost_usd":...}). The harness feeds r.output back as next-turn context on live-loop-harness.mjs:138. So the real multi-turn --run path injects the JSON wrapper metadata as context instead of j.result (the agent actual response text). Fix: parse j.result from the already-parsed object and expose it as output, e.g. `output: p.result ?? p.rawResult ?? out.slice(0,400)` — requires parseClaudeResult to also return the result field, or inline the JSON.parse here.

findings.desc: signal-honoring: real-loop-agent.mjs:33 uses execFileSync which is synchronous and blocks the Node.js event loop for the entire duration of the claude invocation. This makes the harness Promise.race watchdog in live-loop-harness.mjs:113-118 unable to fire while execFileSync runs (timers cannot execute on a blocked event loop). Consequently: (a) transcript.timedOut can never be set by the harness-level watchdog for real claude turns; (b) ac.abort() from the harness never fires during a live turn. The child IS killed — by execFileSync own timeout param — but the harness-level abort-signal contract is broken. A hung or very slow claude call will block the entire process, not just the current turn. The entry-check signal.aborted (line 29) only helps if abort was signaled before the turn starts. Fix: use spawnSync or spawn+stream instead, or a Worker thread, so the event loop remains unblocked and the Promise.race can actually preempt.

findings.desc: [codex-host2 C3/C4] signal honoring inadequate: makeRealLoopAgent uses blocking execFileSync, so the harness Promise.race timer + ac.abort() can't fire mid-call; the child is bounded only by execFileSync's 700s timeout, NOT the AbortSignal (the entry-check only catches already-aborted). FIX: make the agent async via execFile with {signal} so AbortController.abort() actually kills the child + the event loop isn't blocked -> the harness watchdog/turnTimeoutMs become real. (Corroborates quality F-002.)
